found: HIGH, FIXED: a SKU shared by two catalogues got one catalogue's price on both and the other row was lost every night (the 'disagree' guard used all(), not narrowing). Now the row's catalogue id narrows the SKU's listings; a row naming none for a SKU in several catalogues is not read. Check went red first.

HIGH, FIXED: the catalogue-id fallback spread one product's price over every product in the catalogue. Now it matches only when the catalogue's listings are one SKU (sizes of one product); otherwise the row is not read, by line. Check went red first.
LOW, FIXED: a price cell was read loosely ('12%' read as 12). Now plainly an amount (optional rupee sign, digits, commas, two decimals, below ten million) or the row is not read.

MEDIUM, NOT FIXED, SAID: the shared note writer (firestore_door.a_listing_notes_sink, also used for Amazon fees) writes only when a figure changed, so a newer file confirming the same price leaves priceAsOf on the older day and a late older file could then overwrite it. Files are read oldest first and pricing cannot be fetched for past days, so a late older file is rare; changing the shared writer is outside this job. Named for the owner of the sink.

LOW, NOT FIXED, SAID: tables.js neutralises a leading = + - @ in cells with a quote, so a SKU or title starting that way will not match exactly (falls to the next match layer or is reported unmatched).
LOW, NOT FIXED, SAID: with a short pager plus a torn row, the error blames the pager count instead of the torn row (read still refused, nothing saved).

Checked and sound: the short-pager rule accepts only when the page's own count equals the rows read, product performance gets the same rule under the same equality, missing/unreadable catalogue leaves the pricing file unread, side files are taken after listing files, a partial file takes nothing back, masked writes never touch the listing, blank recommended is null, take-back removes all three figures.
